per cent to 6 per cent but was three or lour that is, the Okanagan Telephone Company points. It was also explained that the cost of and the British Columbia Telephone Cornfinancing .a major issue like this is consider- pany?
able and that what the company does is to Mr. Jung. There are other smalier ones, offer shares to its shareholders at a price but tjjejr activities are confined more to the which takes into account the cost of financing. interior Qf Britigh Columbia.
On what page of the evidence is that? Come on.
I cannot give the page.
I will call you on that.

When the president of the
company was asked I believe he said four to six points.
Five to six.

It was points, not percentage. Secondly, any fair comparison would be a comparison of rates charged in cities of equivalent size. In that regard I may say that the rates charged are equivalent to those charged in other places across Canada. I was just trying to get the record straight for the members who were not in the committee.
So am I, so give page references in the committee evidence.

It seemed as though C.C.F. members were trying to drag out something which was pretty bad. This company pays Anglo-Canadian supply company about three-quarters of one per cent, I believe, to do their purchasing. They pay the installation costs.
Now, a great deal was said about United States control. Yes, it is controlled from the United States but the staff is 100 per cent Canadian and that is a lot more than can be said about other companies which are controlled from the United States. The company is operated for the good of the province and it is operated by Canadians. I believe it is operated in a right and proper manner.

The hon. member for Yorkton earlier asked a question as to the number of times applications had been made to the board of transport commissioners for an increase in tariff rates. My information is that the last increase was made in 1953. There have been no applications since that time. I believe that in the last ten years that has been the only application. I say that subject to confirmation from the head office in Vancouver.
What was the amount of the increase in 1953?
I shall include that in my reply.
Are there any more than two telephone companies in British Columbia,

Far be it from me to anticipate the time when all independent telephone companies will be out of existence, yet I believe the committee fully realizes that these independent telephone companies which we have across Canada form the only competition which the larger companies have. I believe also that we are of the opinion we should not put anything in the way of assisting these different companies, both the larger ones such as the British Columbia Telephone Company and the smaller independent companies, in furthering their services to the people. British Columbia is a rapidly expanding province. We have to realize fully the service the telephone company is required to give. I am sure it is not the desire of any member in this house to block this bill because I am sure its passage will contribute much to the services rendered to the people of British Columbia. In addition, the passage of the bill will contribute much to employment across that province. I am sure that when this bill is passed the company will immediately promote the installations which will give better service to the residents of that province.

The house in committee on Bill No. 31, respecting the Rio de Janeiro Tramway, Light and Power Company, Limited-Mr. Morton- Mr. Casselman in the chair.
Clause 1 agreed to.
On clause 2-

speakerposition: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister of Trade and Commerce
maintopic: RIO DE JANEIRO TRAMWAY, LIGHT AND POWER COMPANY, LIMITED
speechtext:
Section 2 contains a provision requiring the change of head office of the company to be sanctioned by the unanimous vote of all the shareholders present in person or represented by proxy at a special general meeting of shareholders duly called for the purpose at which at least 99 per cent of all the issued and outstanding shares in the capital stock of the company are represented. It seems to me that this constitutes a rather extraordinary provision to require, for any corporate action, the unanimous vote

of the shareholders. There may be some special reason for such provision in this bill and the companion bills, and I wonder if the sponsor could tell us what the reason may be.

maintopic: RIO DE JANEIRO TRAMWAY, LIGHT AND POWER COMPANY, LIMITED
speechtext: Perhaps it may sound rather a stringent regulation, but under the circumstances, since this company and the two other subsidiary companies mentioned in the other bills are solely owned by the Brazilian Traction, Light and Power Company Limited, there is no practical problem that arises. This company owns all the shares and therefore, I presume, they have the complete say. I suppose if there were circumstances where there were a number of shareholders we should perhaps look into the principle involved to see if it were too stringent.

Clause agreed to.
